newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Meyer urges banks to back local development.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Meyer urges banks to back local development.

text.p: Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer on Wednesday urged banks to remain responsive to community development needs as they continue a major restructuring that is leading to more centralization.

In a speech prepared for delivery to the annual meeting of Neighborhood Housing Services of New York City, Meyer noted a divergence between the needs of community development and the direction that the banking industry was taking.
He added that with big federal programs to help communities "probably a thing of the past," communities need local private-sector participation more than ever.
A text of Meyer's remarks was issued in Washington.
Meyer said banks and other financial institutions were being allowed to offer a wider variety of financial products, while geographic restraints on their activites are falling away.

"As a result, mergers and acquisitions are increasing and larger banking companies are moving interstate at a rapid pace," Meyer noted. "So while public policy and community development continues to move in a decentralized direction, banking is becoming increasingly centralized."

He said bankers face "a major challenge" to balance efforts to foster development in local communities that use their banking services with the need to show short-term gains for shareholders and to please changing owners.
Meyer urged banks to commit themselves to boost not just "the higher end of the low- and moderate-income market" but all the communities that need financial help to foster revitalization efforts.
